brief.audience: Commercial finance leadership and Chief Revenue Officer (CRO)
brief.purpose: Investigate valuable revenue growth, regional/account performance, and contribution in a synthetic business-device slice informed by Apple disclosures.
questions: Which product and territory combinations grow revenue and contribution together?
Where do pricing, mix, fulfillment and returns weaken growth?
Which account declines warrant recovery versus further discovery?
constraints: Apple is the research target, not a source of private transaction records.
Reported financial totals are context, not targets for this B2B slice.
No implication that Apple has the specific CRO role or simulated commercial problems.

claims.statement: Public sources reviewed do not establish the proposed account/purchaser identities, transaction prices, SKU costs, service failures or product-by-region B2B sales.

blueprint.slice: 50,000 synthetic order lines, January 2024–June 2026. iPhone, MacBook Air and iPad Air sold to fictional business accounts in the US, UK, India and mainland China. Regions roll up to Americas, Europe and Greater China; Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific remain reference context. Start with 300 accounts and 2–5 purchasers per account (proposed).
exclusions: Services, Wearables, retail-consumer identities, inventory and competitor claims
Reconciliation of this small B2B slice to Apple company-wide totals
Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific transaction populations in the first slice
Exact model/configuration catalog until availability dates are verified
Private Apple costs, account records, sales territories and forecasts
blueprint.economic_policy: USD synthetic reporting prices and costs; no inferred FX gains. Gross profit = net sales minus effective product cost; contribution further subtracts allocated fulfillment and variable program costs. Refund plus restocking less recoverable cost is applied once. Decimal cent rounding, reconciliation to source shipment amounts, unknown cost blocks profit claims. Apple gross margin is context, not demo contribution. Show calendar-month YoY and matched/new/lost cohorts; Apple fiscal-year figures remain separately labeled. No realized action benefit is asserted.
blueprint.overlap_policy: One account cohort can participate in cost pressure and promotion. Store affected line IDs; baseline, each isolated mechanism and combined runs share stable random streams. Combined-minus-baseline effect minus isolated effects is the interaction residual. Never add overlapping opportunity estimates. Revision v0.3 adds heterogeneous account size, acquisition ramp-up, temporary dormancy and sustained purchase inactivity as structural baseline dynamics. These coexist with all three mechanisms; no lifecycle causal contrast is asserted.

stories.title: Growth that does not translate into contribution
stories.mechanism: Simulate increased cost on selected devices plus richer low-margin mix and expedited delivery; retain healthy-growth peers. Manufacturing news motivates a supply-cost question but establishes none of these effects.
stories.scope: Selected US and UK business-device cohorts
stories.timing: Synthetic cost event January 2026; compare January–June 2026 with the same 2025 months.
stories.effect_bounds: Proposed affected cohort sales YoY +5% to +15%; contribution YoY -5% to -20%.
stories.comparison_basis: Observed matched-period YoY and plan/peer comparisons remain separate from evaluator-only baseline causal effects.
operational_evidence: Order-line product, account, purchaser, territory and channel keys
Effective costs, shipment allocations and linked returns
Account plans and routine customer activity
prohibited_claims: These losses or service issues actually occurred at Apple
Competitor loss or definitive churn without evidence
YoY or nonpromotion benchmark gaps prove causal lift

stories.title: A few accounts explain a territory shortfall
stories.mechanism: Simulate weaker purchasing at two mainland-China accounts. One has preceding unresolved delivery issues; the other has no supported explanation. Aggregate all purchasers and show stable comparison accounts.
stories.scope: Two synthetic accounts in a Greater China territory
stories.timing: Synthetic disruption February 2025; purchasing falls after 30 days; compare equal months and plan.
stories.effect_bounds: Each affected account sales -20% to -35%; unaffected matched-account cohort -5% to +10%.
stories.comparison_basis: Observed matched-period YoY and plan/peer comparisons remain separate from evaluator-only baseline causal effects.
operational_evidence: Order-line product, account, purchaser, territory and channel keys
Effective costs, shipment allocations and linked returns
Account plans and routine customer activity
alternatives: Purchase timing or normal refresh cycles
A buyer-role change with incomplete context
prohibited_claims: These losses or service issues actually occurred at Apple
Competitor loss or definitive churn without evidence
YoY or nonpromotion benchmark gaps prove causal lift

stories.title: Device refresh volume grows, but offer economics vary
stories.mechanism: Inspired by the lower MacBook Air entry price, simulate a distinct B2B offer with volume response, discounts, program expense, expedited shipments and returns; some cohorts stay profitable.
stories.scope: MacBook Air cohorts across US, UK and India
stories.timing: Synthetic offer April–June 2025, after March 12 availability; eligible generation mapping must be verified.
stories.effect_bounds: Promoted-cohort units +10% to +25% against private baseline; at least one cohort contribution below zero, one above zero.
stories.comparison_basis: Observed matched-period YoY and plan/peer comparisons remain separate from evaluator-only baseline causal effects.
